reviews.rationale: A route-entry role does not determine the child component's interaction-port contract.
Locating Page in the route tree does not explain why replacement changes the selected child.
The role locates route coordination but does not fully account for stability under child replacement.
Contextual role occupancy does not determine whether guard behavior remains stable.
A route-entry role does not account for committing a request that differs from the guard result.
A composition-root role does not account for a blocked request reaching a different destination.
The guard Rule does not define the replacement screen's onNext and onBack contract.
Guard behavior does not explain the identity change of the selected rendered child.
The guard Rule constrains reachable routes but does not fully explain route coordination stability.
The unchanged guard Rule directly accounts for stable allowed and redirect behavior.
The Rule supplies the guard result but does not alone account for the later commit bypass.
The guard Rule directly accounts for why bypassing a blocked result reaches a different destination.
Callback orchestration directly accounts for preserving the declared next and back interaction ports.
